Let  
\[
p(\lambda)=\prod_{j=1}^6(1-\eta_j\lambda).
\]
Then \(p\) is a real polynomial of degree at most \(6\), satisfies \(p(0)=1\), and all its roots are positive.

Set
\[
z(\lambda)=\frac{(\lambda-\frac92)^2-\frac{37}{4}}{3}.
\]
For \(\lambda\in[1,2]\cup[7,8]\), one has \(z(\lambda)\in[-1,1]\). Indeed,
\[
z(1)=z(8)=1,\qquad z(2)=z(7)=-1.
\]

Let \(T_3(t)=4t^3-3t\), and define
\[
p_*(\lambda)=\frac{T_3(z(\lambda))}{T_3(11/3)}.
\]
Since \(z(0)=11/3\), we have \(p_*(0)=1\). Also, for \(z\in[-1,1]\),
\[
|T_3(z)|\le 1,
\]
so
\[
\max_{\lambda\in E}|p_*(\lambda)|
=\frac1{T_3(11/3)}.
\]

Now
\[
T_3\!\left(\frac{11}{3}\right)
=4\left(\frac{11}{3}\right)^3-3\left(\frac{11}{3}\right)
=\frac{5324}{27}-\frac{297}{27}
=\frac{5027}{27}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\max_{\lambda\in E}|p_*(\lambda)|=\frac{27}{5027}.
\]

It remains to prove optimality. The extrema of \(T_3\) occur at
\[
z=1,\ \frac12,\ -\frac12,\ -1,
\]
where the values are respectively
\[
1,-1,1,-1.
\]
Their preimages in \(E\), listed increasingly, are
\[
1<a<b<2<7<9-b<9-a<8,
\]
with
\[
p_*=\rho,-\rho,\rho,-\rho,-\rho,\rho,-\rho,\rho,
\qquad \rho=\frac{27}{5027}.
\]

Suppose another degree-\(\le6\) polynomial \(p\) with \(p(0)=1\) satisfied
\[
\max_{\lambda\in E}|p(\lambda)|<\rho.
\]
Then \(r=p-p_*\) has alternating signs at the eight points above, producing six distinct zeros of \(r\), one in each of
\[
(1,a),(a,b),(b,2),(7,9-b),(9-b,9-a),(9-a,8).
\]
Moreover,
\[
r(0)=p(0)-p_*(0)=0.
\]
Thus \(r\) has at least seven distinct zeros, impossible for a nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(6\). Hence every admissible polynomial satisfies
\[
\max_{\lambda\in E}|p(\lambda)|\ge \rho.
\]

Finally, \(p_*\) is admissible for the gradient iteration: the roots of \(T_3\) are
\[
0,\quad \pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2},
\]
and their six preimages under \(z(\lambda)\) are positive. Thus \(p_*\) factors as
\[
p_*(\lambda)=\prod_{j=1}^6(1-\eta_j\lambda)
\]
with all \(\eta_j>0\).

Therefore,
\[
\boxed{\rho_6=\frac{27}{5027}}.
\]
